title: Master JavaScript + React.js Interview Coding Programs
audience: Senior JavaScript / React Developer Interview Preparation
focus: Programming questions only, with examples, complete solutions, explanations, and interview tips.

questions.title: Reverse a String
questions.question: Reverse the string 'hello' so the output is 'olleh'.

questions.title: Check Palindrome
questions.question: Check whether a string reads the same forward and backward. Example: 'madam' => true.

questions.title: Find Largest Number
questions.question: Find the largest number in [10, 5, 30, 8, 20].

questions.title: Find Second Largest Number
questions.question: Find the second largest distinct number in [10, 5, 30, 8, 20].

questions.title: Remove Duplicates
questions.question: Remove duplicate values from [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4].

questions.title: Find Duplicate Values
questions.question: Find values occurring more than once in [1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 3].

questions.title: Character Frequency
questions.question: Count how many times each character appears in a string such as 'hello'.

questions.title: Word Frequency
questions.question: Count the frequency of each word in 'hello world hello'.

questions.title: Find Missing Number
questions.question: Find the missing number from [1, 2, 3, 5, 6], assuming numbers should be 1 through 6.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.question: Return the indices of two numbers whose sum equals the target. Example: [2,7,11,15], target 9 => [0,1].

questions.title: Move Zeros to End
questions.question: Move all zeros to the end while preserving the order of non-zero values. Example: [0,1,0,3,12] => [1,3,12,0,0].

questions.title: Intersection of Two Arrays
questions.question: Find common values between [1,2,3,4] and [3,4,5,6].

questions.title: Union of Two Arrays
questions.question: Return unique values from both arrays. Example: [1,2,3] and [2,3,4] => [1,2,3,4].

questions.title: Flatten Nested Array
questions.question: Flatten [1, [2, [3, [4]]]] without using Array.prototype.flat().

questions.title: Maximum Occurring Element
questions.question: Find the element occurring most frequently in [1,3,2,3,4,3,2].

questions.title: Group Objects by Property
questions.question: Group users by department.

questions.title: Sort Objects by Age
questions.question: Sort an array of user objects by age in ascending order.
questions.solution:
const result = users.sort((a, b) => a.age - b.age);

console.log(result);

questions.title: Implement map()
questions.question: Implement a custom Array.prototype.myMap().

questions.title: Implement filter()
questions.question: Implement a custom Array.prototype.myFilter().

questions.title: Implement reduce()
questions.question: Implement a custom Array.prototype.myReduce() supporting an optional initial value.

questions.title: Debounce
questions.question: Implement debounce(fn, delay) so only the final call runs after the caller stops invoking the function for the delay period.

questions.title: Throttle
questions.question: Implement throttle(fn, delay) so the function executes at most once per delay interval.

questions.title: Deep Clone
questions.question: Create a true independent copy of a nested object so changes to nested properties in the copy do not affect the original.

questions.title: Memoization
questions.question: Implement memoize(fn) so repeated calls with the same arguments return a cached result.

questions.title: Currying
questions.question: Convert add(a,b,c) into a curried function supporting curriedAdd(1)(2)(3), curriedAdd(1,2)(3), and curriedAdd(1)(2,3).

questions.title: Closure Counter
questions.question: Create a counter whose private count persists across calls.

questions.title: Fix var + setTimeout Closure
questions.question: Fix the loop so it prints 0, 1, 2 instead of 3, 3, 3.
questions.key_concept: var scope, let block scope, closures

questions.title: Event Loop Output
questions.question: Predict the output and explain the order of synchronous code, Promise microtasks, and setTimeout macrotasks.

questions.title: Promise.all Polyfill
questions.question: Implement a simplified Promise.all that preserves input order and rejects if any input rejects.

questions.title: Query String to Object
questions.question: Convert 'name=Ram&age=30&city=Pune' into an object.

questions.title: Object to Query String
questions.question: Convert {name:'Ram', age:30, city:'Pune'} into 'name=Ram&age=30&city=Pune'.

questions.title: Flatten Object
questions.question: Flatten nested object keys using dot notation. Example: user.address.city => 'user.address.city'.

questions.title: Remove Property Without Mutation
questions.question: Remove password from an object without changing the original object.

questions.title: Find Longest Word
questions.question: Find the longest word in 'JavaScript is powerful language'.

questions.title: useDebounce Hook
questions.question: Create a React useDebounce hook that returns a value only after it has remained unchanged for the specified delay.

questions.title: usePrevious Hook
questions.question: Create a hook that returns the previous render's value.

questions.title: Search with Debounce
questions.question: Build a search flow where typing waits 500ms before making the API request.

questions.title: Pagination
questions.question: Implement pagination state with page, page size, loading, error handling, Previous, Next, and numbered pages.

questions.title: Autocomplete with Keyboard Navigation
questions.question: Build an autocomplete flow: input -> debounce -> API -> suggestions -> keyboard navigation.

questions.title: Infinite Scroll
questions.question: Implement infinite scrolling using IntersectionObserver instead of continuously listening to the scroll event.

questions.title: Closure Output
questions.question: Predict the output of a function that declares var x outside and inside another function.

questions.title: Temporal Dead Zone
questions.question: Explain what happens when accessing a let variable before its declaration.

questions.title: typeof Questions
questions.question: Predict the results of typeof null, typeof undefined, typeof [], and typeof {}.

questions.title: == vs ===
questions.question: Explain the results of loose equality versus strict equality.

questions.title: Object Reference Equality
questions.question: Why are two separately created empty objects not strictly equal?

questions.title: Reference vs Value
questions.question: Predict the output when two variables reference the same object and one modifies a property.

questions.title: Implement Promise.race
questions.question: Implement a simplified Promise.race that settles when the first input promise settles.

questions.title: Sequential API Calls
questions.question: Call API URLs one after another rather than concurrently.

questions.title: Limit Concurrent API Calls
questions.question: Given many async tasks, execute no more than a fixed number concurrently.

questions.title: API Search with AbortController
questions.question: Prevent stale autocomplete/search requests from updating state after a newer request starts.
Create a counter with Increment, Decrement, and Reset buttons using useState.
questions.explanation: useState stores the current count. Functional updates are safe when the new state depends on the previous state.
questions.interview_tip: Explain why setCount(c => c + 1) is preferable to setCount(count + 1) when multiple updates may be batched.

questions.question: Build a Todo component that can add and remove todos.

example.output: Todo appears and can be removed

questions.explanation: The input is controlled by state. Adding creates a new array instead of mutating the existing state; filtering removes an item immutably.
questions.interview_tip: Be ready to explain why a stable unique key is important when rendering lists.

questions.question: Create a toggle button that switches between ON and OFF.
questions.explanation: The functional state update flips the previous boolean value.
questions.interview_tip: This is a simple test of state and event handling.

questions.question: Filter a list of users based on a search input.
questions.explanation: Filtering is derived from the current search state; there is no need to store filtered users separately.
questions.interview_tip: Explain why derived data generally should not be duplicated in state.

questions.question: Create a search component that waits 500ms after typing stops before calling the API.

example.output: One API call after 500ms of inactivity

questions.explanation: Every keystroke creates a timer. Cleanup cancels the previous timer, so only the final input after 500ms triggers the request.
questions.interview_tip: The key concept is useEffect cleanup and why debounce reduces API calls.

questions.question: Implement a reusable useDebounce(value, delay) custom hook.

example.output: Returned value changes after the delay

questions.explanation: The hook delays propagation of the latest value and cleans up the previous timer.
questions.interview_tip: A common follow-up is to use this hook with an API search.

questions.question: Create a hook that returns the previous value from the previous render.

example.output: On the 20 render, previous value is 10

questions.explanation: useRef persists between renders without causing a re-render. useEffect updates it after the current render.
questions.interview_tip: Explain why returning ref.current before the effect update gives the previous value.

questions.question: Create a custom hook that stores state in localStorage and restores it on initial load.
questions.explanation: The lazy initializer reads localStorage once during initialization, while the effect persists subsequent state changes.
questions.interview_tip: In Next.js/SSR, mention that localStorage is browser-only and should be accessed safely on the client.

questions.question: Create a reusable hook for fetching data with loading and error state.
questions.explanation: The hook centralizes loading, success, and error handling. The cancellation flag prevents an old request from updating state after the component changes or unmounts.
questions.interview_tip: A stronger production answer can use AbortController instead of only a cancellation flag.

questions.question: Create a custom hook that detects clicks outside a referenced element.
questions.explanation: The document listener checks whether the clicked target is outside the referenced DOM node and is removed during cleanup.
questions.interview_tip: Mention cleanup to avoid event-listener leaks.

questions.question: Implement client-side pagination with Previous, Next, and page numbers.
questions.explanation: The start index is calculated from page and pageSize, then slice selects the visible records.
questions.interview_tip: For server-side pagination, send page and pageSize to the API instead of slicing the full dataset.

questions.question: Load the next page when the user reaches the bottom using IntersectionObserver.
questions.explanation: IntersectionObserver detects when the sentinel enters the viewport without repeatedly handling scroll events.
questions.interview_tip: Discuss preventing duplicate requests while loading and stopping when hasMore is false.

questions.question: Create a reusable modal with open/close behavior and an overlay.
questions.explanation: The overlay closes the modal, while stopPropagation prevents clicks inside the dialog from reaching the overlay.
questions.interview_tip: For production, discuss focus management, Escape handling, portals, and accessibility.

questions.question: Create tabs where clicking a tab displays its corresponding content.
questions.explanation: Only the active tab id needs to be stored in state; content is derived from the tabs configuration.
questions.interview_tip: For accessible tabs, mention ARIA roles and keyboard navigation.

questions.question: Create an accordion where clicking a question expands or collapses its answer.
questions.explanation: openId identifies the currently expanded item. Clicking the same item closes it.
questions.interview_tip: For multiple-open accordions, store a Set or array of open ids instead.

questions.question: Implement a list of checkboxes with Select All and individual selection.
questions.explanation: selected is the source of truth. Select All either selects every item or clears the selection.
questions.interview_tip: A production version may need an indeterminate state when some but not all items are selected.

questions.question: Create a stopwatch with Start, Stop, and Reset buttons.
questions.explanation: The interval exists only while running is true and is cleared whenever running changes or the component unmounts.
questions.interview_tip: Always mention cleanup of intervals.

questions.question: Create a simple controlled login form with required email and password validation.
questions.explanation: The form is controlled by React state. Validation builds a new errors object and submission occurs only when there are no errors.
questions.interview_tip: Be ready to explain controlled versus uncontrolled inputs.

questions.question: Build a multi-step form with Next, Back, and final Submit behavior.
questions.explanation: The step number controls which section is displayed while one shared form object preserves values across steps.
questions.interview_tip: Mention step-specific validation before allowing Next.

questions.question: Build a shopping cart that adds products, increases/decreases quantity, removes items, and calculates total.
questions.explanation: Cart updates are immutable. The total is derived from cart and memoized to avoid recalculating when unrelated state changes.
questions.interview_tip: Discuss whether useMemo is actually needed based on calculation cost.

questions.question: Create a helper that retries a failed API request a fixed number of times.

example.output: Up to 4 total attempts if the initial attempt is counted separately

questions.explanation: The loop retries after failures and throws the last error when the retry limit is exhausted.
questions.interview_tip: A stronger production solution may add exponential backoff and retry only transient errors.

questions.question: Cancel an in-flight fetch when the query changes or the component unmounts.
questions.explanation: Each effect creates an AbortController. Cleanup aborts the request associated with the previous query.
questions.interview_tip: This prevents stale requests from competing with newer requests and reduces wasted network work.

questions.question: Memoize an expensive derived calculation so it only recalculates when its input changes.

example.output: Filtering doesn't rerun when only counter changes

questions.explanation: The filtered array is recomputed only when products or search changes.
questions.interview_tip: Do not say useMemo automatically makes every component faster; explain the tradeoff and use it for meaningful expensive work.

questions.question: Prevent a memoized child from rerendering because a callback prop gets a new function reference on every parent render.

example.output: Child can skip rerender when callback dependency is unchanged

questions.explanation: React.memo can skip a child render when props are shallowly equal. useCallback keeps the function reference stable.
questions.interview_tip: Explain that useCallback is useful only when referential equality matters, such as memoized children or hook dependencies.

questions.question: Implement a counter using useReducer with increment, decrement, and reset actions.
questions.explanation: useReducer centralizes state transitions as explicit actions, which is useful when state logic becomes more complex.
questions.interview_tip: Compare useReducer with useState and explain when reducer-based state becomes easier to maintain.

questions.question: Render nested comments recursively when each comment can contain replies.
questions.explanation: The component calls itself for each reply, naturally matching the recursive data structure.
questions.interview_tip: This pattern also applies to file trees, menus, organizational charts, and nested categories.

questions.question: Create a recursive tree component with expandable/collapsible nodes.

example.output: Click folder expands or collapses children

questions.explanation: Each node owns its expanded state and recursively renders children.
questions.interview_tip: For very large trees, discuss virtualization and avoiding unnecessary rerenders.

questions.question: Implement basic drag-and-drop reordering of a list using native HTML drag events.
questions.explanation: The dragged index is stored, and on drop the array is copied and the item is moved using splice.
questions.interview_tip: Know that production drag-and-drop often needs better accessibility and touch support.

questions.question: Create a file input that validates file type/size and uploads the selected file using FormData.
questions.explanation: The browser File object provides type and size information. FormData sends multipart form data to the server.
questions.interview_tip: Mention that client-side validation improves UX but server-side validation is still mandatory.

questions.question: Create a countdown timer that starts from 10 and stops at zero.
questions.explanation: The interval decrements state once per second and is cleaned up when stopped or when the effect reruns.
questions.interview_tip: Be careful with stale state inside intervals; functional state updates avoid that problem.

questions.question: Create a form where users can dynamically add and remove phone-number fields.

example.output: Three phone inputs total if one existed initially

questions.explanation: The form stores fields as an array and uses immutable map/filter/spread operations to update it.
questions.interview_tip: If fields can be reordered or persisted, use stable IDs instead of array indexes as keys.

questions.question: Execute many async API tasks while allowing at most five tasks to run concurrently.

example.output: No more than 5 requests active at once

questions.explanation: A fixed number of worker functions pull the next task index until all tasks are completed.
questions.interview_tip: This is a strong senior-level question because it tests promises, concurrency, closures, and ordering.

questions.question: Update UI immediately for a like action, then roll back if the API request fails.

example.output: UI changes immediately; failure restores previous state

questions.explanation: The UI changes before the server responds. If the request fails, the previous state is restored.
questions.interview_tip: Discuss race conditions if users can trigger multiple mutations before earlier requests finish.

questions.question: Lazy-load a React component and display a fallback while it loads.
questions.explanation: React.lazy splits the component into a separate chunk and Suspense displays fallback UI while the chunk loads.
questions.interview_tip: Connect this to route-level code splitting for large applications.

questions.question: Create a class-based Error Boundary that shows fallback UI when a descendant throws during rendering.
questions.explanation: Error boundaries catch rendering/lifecycle errors in descendant components and allow fallback UI instead of crashing the whole tree.
questions.interview_tip: Mention that traditional Error Boundaries are class components and do not catch every kind of asynchronous event error.
